commit_message: [entropy_src] Add CSR to control one-way behavior of threshold registers
justification: The commit adds a new CSR (THRESHOLD_ONEWAY) that controls threshold register one-way behavior. The scoreboard's predict_one_way_threshold function now conditionally applies one-way constraints based on THRESHOLD_ONEWAY value (lines show `one_way_threshold = `gmv(ral.threshold_oneway) != MuBi4False`), requiring updated sequences to exercise this new control knob and coverage points to track the new alert bit. The scoreboard must now synchronize its reference model to the conditional one-way behavior.

commit_message: [entropy_src] Unify FIPS and bypass threshold registers to save area
justification: The RTL unified FIPS and bypass threshold registers into single threshold registers, eliminating separate fips_thresh and bypass_thresh fields. The DV diff shows explicit RAL reference updates in entropy_src_scoreboard.sv (removing fips_mode parameter and field accesses) and entropy_src_cov_if.sv (register name constant updates), indicating both register model desynchronization and scoreboard reference model behavioral changes to match the unified register architecture.

commit_message: [otbn] Increase DMEM to 32KiB
justification: The DMEM address width parameter change from 12 to 15 bits in otbn_trace_if.sv breaks the DV interface contract, and the memory size increase (4096 to 32768 bytes) in otbn_memutil.cc affects how DV utilities interact with memory. Sequences that hardcode memory addresses or assumptions about DMEM size will fail with the new 32KiB DMEM layout.

justification: The IMEM size increase from 8KiB to 16KiB requires updates to DV component parameters and constants that encode explicit knowledge of the memory interface. The trace interface parameter ImemAddrWidth changes from 13 to 14 bits, and the memutil C++ utility updates the IMEM word count from 8192/4 to 16384/4, reflecting a structural interface change that breaks any DV components relying on the old memory dimensions.

commit_message: [aes/dv] Test GHASH.FSM.LOCAL_ESC countermeasure
justification: The commit adds a new fault injection test sequence (aes_ghash_fi_vseq.sv) that depends on new DV-specific interface signals and fault injection capabilities (fi_ghash_if.sv). The sequence references RTL state enum values (aes_pkg::GHASH_IDLE, aes_pkg::GHASH_MULT, etc.) and invokes fault injection methods on cfg.aes_ghash_fi_vif that must align with the updated error injection interface. Any mismatch between the sequence's assumptions about injectable signals and the actual interface definition would render the sequence structurally invalid.

justification: The DPI-C function interface c_dpi_aes_crypt_message has been modified with new parameters (data_len_i, aad_len_i, crypto_res), breaking the DPI function signature. The scoreboard calls this function but has been updated to match the new interface; however, any other DV components calling the old interface will fail (INTERFACE_DRIFT). Additionally, the reference model behavior has changed to return error codes and handle explicit length parameters instead of deriving them from array sizes, which may affect scoreboard predictions for GCM mode tag mismatch scenarios (CHECKER_DESYNC).

commit_message: [entropy_src] Only use a single watermark register to reduce area
justification: The commit removes multiple watermark registers (9 total, one per health test) and replaces them with a single shared watermark register controlled by a new HT_WATERMARK_NUM CSR. The DV scoreboard's `update_watermark()` function signature changed (removed fips_mode parameter, added disabling parameter) and its logic was rewritten to check if the selected test matches ht_watermark_num before updating. Sequences that accessed individual watermark registers now need refactoring, and the RAL model requires explicit updates to reflect the new register structure.

commit_message: [otbn,dv] Model the local escalation registering in the tracer
justification: The DV tracer module now registers (pipelines by one cycle) the integrity error signals before feeding them to the internal_intg_err_i interface. Any scoreboard or reference model that was checking these signals combinatorially will now be misaligned with the updated design behavior, as the error signals will appear one cycle later than previously modeled.

commit_message: [otbn,rtl] Clean up naming of predecoded signals
justification: The commit renames predecoded signal ports from `*_predec_bignum` to `*_bignum_predec` across multiple RTL modules. The DV diff shows breaking changes in testbench files that directly reference these signal names via hierarchical paths in sequence code (otbn_ctrl_redun_vseq.sv using uvm_hdl_read) and tracer interface bindings (otbn_trace_if.sv accessing internal signals). These signal name changes break both assertion/binding paths and sequence HDL access patterns.

commit_message: [aes] Integrate GHASH module into design and interface main controller
justification: The RTL diff adds new control signals (ghash_in_valid_o, ghash_in_ready_i, ghash_out_valid_i, ghash_out_ready_o, ghash_load_hash_subkey_o, data_out_sel_o) to the aes_control module interface and introduces an AESGCMEnable parameter. New control interface signals require corresponding driver, monitor, and sequence updates.

commit_message: [aes] Extend CSRs for AES-GCM support
justification: The commit adds new CSR fields (ctrl_gcm_shadowed register with phase and num_valid_bytes fields) and introduces new GCM-phase-dependent validation logic in aes_common_vseq.sv. The sequence now conditionally validates the new ctrl_gcm_shadowed register based on current phase state, and the RAL model must reflect the new register structure and field definitions. New helper function ctrl_gcm_reg_map_invalid_value() enforces phase-transition constraints that were not previously modeled.

commit_message: [csrng] Use the correct counter widths in csrng_err_vseq

commit_message: [entropy_src/rtl] Absorb full window before triggering SHA3 processing
justification: The DV diff removes an assertoff directive for `FifosEmptyWhenShaProcess_A`, indicating that the RTL behavioral fix (delaying SHA3 processing until FIFOs are drained) now makes the previously disabled assertion valid. This means DV assertions that were orphaned/disabled due to the bug are now being re-enabled, and the scoreboard reference model may need updates to reflect the new pipeline timing behavior around SHA3 processing triggers.

commit_message: [entropy_src] Lock up Ack SM upon fatal local events, align scoreboard

The scoreboard's reference model has been updated to reflect this behavioral change by expanding the error cases that trigger fatal escalation and correcting the error mask to include both main_sm and ack_sm errors. This is a scoreboard realignment with RTL behavioral changes.

commit_message: [hw,keymgr_dpe,rtl] Remove constraint of maximum number of derivation stages

The scoreboard's boot stage increment logic must now handle the new runtime stage and its no-increment behavior, and sequences must adapt their operational constraints that previously checked boot_stage < DpeNumBootStages-1.

commit_message: [hw,keymgr_dpe,rtl] Initialize slots with randomness (and during erase)
justification: The RTL diff changes slot initialization and erasure to use randomness (entropy_i) instead of zeros, but the DV scoreboard still models erasure as setting slots to '0. The scoreboard's reference model no longer matches the actual RTL behavior—it expects erased slots to contain zeros, but the hardware now fills them with random entropy values. The added check_key_slot_erased flag and old_key tracking indicate an attempt to address this, but the fundamental mismatch persists: the scoreboard clears the key to '0 while the RTL randomizes it.

justification: The RTL adds a new input port `lc_hw_debug_clr_i` to rv_dm module. The DV diff shows corresponding updates to the testbench interface (*_if.sv), base sequence (*_base_vseq.sv), and top-level testbench (tb.sv) to expose and drive this new signal. The interface drift is evident from the port addition; sequence invalidation occurs because the base sequence's constraint and update logic must now account for the new `lc_hw_debug_clr` signal with specific semantics (must map 0→Off, not a random non-On value).

commit_message: [top,otp_macro] Move prim_otp out of otp_ctrl
justification: The RTL changed signal types from otp_ctrl_pkg::lc_otp_vendor_test_req_t/rsp_t to otp_macro_pkg::otp_test_req_t/rsp_t, and parameter references from OtpTestCtrlWidth to CsrOtpTestCtrlWidth. The DV diff shows corresponding updates to the interface signals in lc_ctrl_if.sv, tb.sv, and lc_ctrl_env_cfg.sv reflecting these port width and type changes, which is consistent with INTERFACE_DRIFT.

commit_message: [hw,pwm,rtl] Move pwm to ip_templates
justification: This commit is a structural refactoring that moves the entire PWM IP block from hw/ip/pwm/rtl to ip_templates. The DV diff shows wholesale deletion of all DV infrastructure files including the testbench (tb_top.sv), all agent/monitor/driver files, scoreboard, assertions (bind.sv), coverage files (cover.ccf, pwm_unr_excl.vRefine), and all environment packages. This is a complete DV ecosystem migration that invalidates all existing DV components across all categories: interface definitions become stale, test sequences reference a moved design, scoreboard reference models are orphaned, assertion binding paths are broken, and coverage configuration files are deleted.

commit_message: [hw,gpio,rtl] Move gpio to ip_templates
justification: The commit moves the GPIO RTL module to ip_templates, which triggers wholesale deletion of the DV directory structure. The DV diff shows removal of testbench files (*_bind.sv with assertion bindings, coverage exclusion files *_cov_excl.el, and entire environment/testbench hierarchy). This breaks interface knowledge encoded in *_env_pkg.sv, *_if.sv, and DV component references, invalidates assertion binding paths via *_bind.sv, and orphans coverage models from the relocated RTL.

commit_message: [keymgr, keymgr_dpe, rtl] Correct KMAC input for DPE
justification: The RTL introduces a new `DpeAdvDataWidth` parameter that differs from the shared `AdvDataWidth`, and parametrizes `keymgr_kmac_if` with it. The DV scoreboard must update its reference model and data structures to use `DpeAdvDataWidth` instead of `AdvDataWidth` to correctly validate the KMAC input width; failure to align these width calculations in the scoreboard creates checker desynchronization. Additionally, the interface width change (parametrization of keymgr_kmac_if) represents an interface drift that may affect environment configuration.

commit_message: [ipgen,otp_ctrl] Change otp_ctrl to ipgen
justification: This is a massive structural refactor converting otp_ctrl from a traditional RTL IP to an ipgen-templated design. The entire RTL module hierarchy, parameter structure, and port interfaces are being regenerated from templates with ${topname} substitution. The DV diff shows deletion of the legacy testbench README and indicates all DV components (env, interfaces, sequences, monitors, scoreboard, assertions, coverage) must be regenerated or substantially reorganized to account for the new template-based instantiation model where otp_ctrl is now generated per-top (earlgrey, darjeeling). This invalidates explicit design knowledge encoded in DV component interfaces, breaks existing sequences that reference specific module hierarchy and parameters, desynchronizes the scoreboard reference model from the new generated implementation, orphans assertions tied to the old module structure, and renders coverage points misaligned with regenerated RTL.

commit_message: [prim_fifo_sync,rtl] Specialize for Depth == 1
justification: The RTL commit changes prim_fifo_sync assertion macro calls from ASSERT_PRIM_COUNT_ERROR_TRIGGER_ALERT (which targeted individual read/write pointers) to ASSERT_PRIM_FIFO_SYNC_ERROR_TRIGGERS_ALERT1 (a new unified macro). The DV diff shows removal of the splat_fifo_storage() function and dut_init() task from otbn_common_vseq.sv, which were previously needed to support the fault injection testing for the old per-pointer assertions. This represents orphaned test infrastructure tied to assertion paths that have been restructured, requiring testbench updates to align with the new assertion hierarchy.

commit_message: [hw,spi_host,rtl] Make NumCS an exposed  parameter
justification: The RTL change exposes NumCS as a top-level parameter, requiring DV to track this new parametrization. The DV diff shows: (1) Interface drift: tb.sv and spi_host_env_pkg.sv updated to use SPI_HOST_NUM_CS instead of hardcoded NumCS, affecting environment configuration; (2) Assertion orphaning: spi_host_bind.sv and spi_host_data_stable_sva.sv modified to parameterize NumCS, indicating assertions must now be bound with the correct parameter value from the new env_cfg_pkg.

commit_message: [hw,prim,ram_1p] Add DFT response channel
justification: The RTL interface changed significantly: the single `ram_cfg_i` port was split into separate `ram_cfg_imem_i` and `ram_cfg_dmem_i` inputs, and two new output ports `ram_cfg_rsp_imem_o` and `ram_cfg_rsp_dmem_o` were added. The DV testbench files (tb.sv, otbn_top_sim.sv) were updated to match, but any DV environment, interface, or driver components that encode explicit knowledge of the original unified ram_cfg interface signature are now misaligned with the updated design.

commit_message: [hw,spi_host,rtl] Remove configopts multi register
justification: The RTL commit removes the multi-register structure for configopts (converting from configopts[i] array to a single configopts register). The DV diff shows widespread changes to UVM sequences that access this register: constraints and register field accesses throughout *_base_vseq.sv are modified from array indexing (cpol[i], clkdiv[i], etc.) to scalar access (cpol, clkdiv). Additionally, RAL register access patterns in program_configopt_regs() changed from ral.configopts[i] to ral.configopts, indicating manual RAL file updates to reflect the register map change.

commit_message: [hw,lc_ctrl,rtl] Make number of RMA ack signals available at top
justification: The commit adds a new parameterizable interface width (NumRmaAckSigs) to lc_ctrl_if.sv, which is a DV interface definition. This requires updates across the DV environment package, virtual interface declarations, testbench instantiation, and sequences that reference this parameter. The change adds explicit knowledge of the interface parameter to multiple DV components, aligning with interface drift mechanism where port/parameter changes break DV components encoding design interface knowledge.

commit_message: [hw,keymgr_dpe,rtl] Remove flash seed input as not used currently
justification: The RTL removal of the flash_i input port and UseOtpSeedsInsteadOfFlash parameter breaks multiple DV components: (1) keymgr_dpe_if.sv loses the flash signal declaration and related initialization/helper functions (INTERFACE_DRIFT); (2) keymgr_dpe_env_pkg.sv removes flash-related invalid input enum values and scoreboard logic depends on flash seed source selection (SEQUENCE_INVALIDATION for tests exercising those invalid input types); (3) keymgr_dpe_scoreboard.sv removes conditional logic selecting between flash and OTP seeds for key derivation, simplifying to OTP-only (CHECKER_DESYNC). The tb.sv instantiation also removes the parameter override.

commit_message: [hw,dma,rtl] Add a chunk done interrupt
justification: The commit adds a new interrupt signal (intr_dma_chunk_done_o) to the DMA module interface, requiring DV updates across multiple layers: (1) env_pkg parameter renumbering of interrupt indices breaks any hardcoded interrupt references; (2) scoreboard must track the new interrupt and update expected behavior; (3) base and generic sequences must handle the new StatusChunkDone completion state and new clear_chunk_done() task; (4) testbench instantiation must connect the new interrupt port.

commit_message: [hw,dma,rtl] Use a status interrupt and interrupt prims
justification: The RTL change replaces inline interrupt logic with prim_intr_hw primitives and changes intr_state register access from W1C to RO. The scoreboard must now predict interrupts differently (clearing status bits instead of writing intr_state), and sequences that explicitly call clear_interrupts() via intr_state writes are structurally invalid.

commit_message: [kmac, rtl/dv/sw] Remove unused error code
justification: The DV diff shows removal of `kmac_pkg::ErrShadowRegUpdate` from the `illegal_bins` coverpoint in kmac_env_cov.sv. This is a coverage model update that reflects the RTL removal of the unused error code, maintaining alignment between the coverage specification and the RTL design.

commit_message: [hw,rv_dm,rtl] Convert DMI to real TL-UL interface
justification: The commit renames DMI port signals from `dmi_tl_h2d_i`/`dmi_tl_d2h_o` to `dbg_tl_d_i`/`dbg_tl_d_o`, breaking explicit port-level dependencies in DV components. The DV bind file and testbench have been updated, but any environment, agent, driver, monitor, or interface definition files that encode these signal names will fail to compile or exhibit incorrect behavior.

commit_message: [lc_ctrl] Convert DMI to real TL-UL interface
justification: The commit renames DMI interface ports from `dmi_tl_h2d_i`/`dmi_tl_d2h_o` to `dmi_tl_i`/`dmi_tl_o`, breaking port references in the testbench binding and assertion modules. The DV changes update tb.sv and lc_ctrl_bind.sv to track the new signal names, but this is a reactive fix indicating an interface drift failure mode where the testbench had to adapt to port renamings.

commit_message: [lc_ctrl] Rename reg block to 'regs'
justification: The commit renames the register block interface from 'tl_i/tl_o' to 'regs_tl_i/regs_tl_o' and updates all related type names (lc_ctrl_reg_block → lc_ctrl_regs_reg_block, lc_ctrl_ral_pkg → lc_ctrl_regs_ral_pkg). This breaks INTERFACE_DRIFT (port names in tb.sv, bind.sv), RAL_DESYNC (manually maintained RAL package imports and type references in *_env_cfg.sv, *_env_pkg.sv, *_scoreboard.sv, *_base_vseq.sv), and ASSERTION_ORPHANING (assertion bind references to renamed signals and reg block names in *_bind.sv). The DV diff shows explicit changes to RAL-related files (env_pkg, env_cfg) that reference the renamed RAL block types.

commit_message: [hw,mbx,rtl/dv] Remove references to obsolete devmode interface
justification: The DV diff removes the `has_devmode` configuration flag from mbx_env_cfg.sv, indicating that the testbench environment configuration previously tracked a devmode interface that is now obsolete. This configuration field encodes explicit knowledge of the design interface; its removal reflects the RTL's elimination of the devmode_i port, causing potential interface drift in DV components that may have relied on this configuration.

commit_message: [gpio] Add snapshot functionality
justification: The RTL adds new port signals (strap_en_i, sampled_straps_o) and new register fields (hw_straps_data_in, hw_straps_data_in_valid) that require testbench interface and sequence updates. The DV diff shows incomplete integration: tb.sv imports gpio_pkg and instantiates the new ports but leaves them undriven (strap_en_i hardcoded to 1'b0) with a TODO comment indicating snapshot functionality testing is not yet implemented. This creates interface drift and renders sequences for testing the new strap sampling feature invalid or missing.

commit_message: [kmac/dv] Add sideload_invalid test.
justification: The commit adds a new test sequence (kmac_sideload_invalid_vseq.sv) that exercises the StKeyMgrErrKeyNotValid FSM state by invalidating the sideload key. The scoreboard was updated to handle this new error condition (cfg.key_invalidated flag) and reorganized its digest verification logic to account for the error path. The test introduces new operational constraints and error injection patterns that affect both the sequence behavior and the reference model.

commit_message: [hw,mbx] Update source files with new license header
justification: This commit updates only license headers across DV files with no functional changes to RTL interfaces, sequences, scoreboards, assertions, coverage, or RAL definitions. The change is purely cosmetic (copyright attribution update) and does not break any DV component logic or structure.

commit_message: [keymgr,keymgr_dpe] Change reseed counter to count PRNG updates instead of cycles
justification: The RTL change introduces a new signal `lfsr_en` that must be captured in the DV testbench interface (*_if.sv). The DV diff shows updates to keymgr_dpe_if.sv adding `lfsr_en` wire and modifying EDN wait counter logic to count PRNG updates instead of cycles, requiring corresponding changes to assertion checks and reference models (*_scoreboard.sv) that track EDN request timing based on the old cycle-counting semantics.

commit_message: [hw,dma,rtl] Only set error code when entering the error state
justification: RTL removal of memory buffer limit interrupt functionality and associated registers breaks DV: (1) test sequence dma_mem_limit_vseq.sv is deleted and referenced in config; (2) scoreboard logic predicting DMA_MEM_LIMIT interrupt is removed; (3) coverage points for dst_addr_limit, dst_addr_almost_limit, and their crosses are deleted; (4) dma_seq_item constraints and fields related to address limits are removed; (5) DMA_MEM_LIMIT constant removed from env_pkg.

commit_message: [dma] Src and dst alignment may differ
justification: The RTL removed the address alignment constraint (source and destination must have same alignment), but the DV constraint in dma_seq_item.sv was updated to reflect this change by replacing the equality constraint with independent per-transfer-width alignment checks. The DV diff shows the sequence item constraints were corrected to match the relaxed RTL behavior, preventing sequence invalidation.

commit_message: [dv,dma] Consistent error bits and register fields
justification: The DV diff shows changes to dma_scoreboard.sv where error code bit indexing is refactored from hardcoded numeric indices (0-7) to named enumeration constants (DmaSourceAddrErr, DmaDestAddrErr, etc.). This is a reference model update that reflects RTL enumeration renaming (DmaDestinationAddrErr → DmaDestAddrErr, DmaCompletionErr → DmaBusErr). The scoreboard's error tracking logic must stay synchronized with the RTL's error enumeration, making this a checker desynchronization scenario.

commit_message: [dv,dma] Test locking of DMA-enabled memory range
justification: RTL changes alter DMA state machine behavior (clearing status bits, SHA digest handling) and register update conditions. The DV diff shows sequence inheritance changes (dma_memory_region_lock_vseq now extends dma_generic_vseq instead of dma_memory_smoke_vseq) and removal of manual status register clearing logic, indicating scoreboard reference model must be updated to track new status clearing behavior. The new virtual task hooks (starting_iter, ending_txn) and constraint modifications suggest sequences depend on prior register state assumptions that have changed.

commit_message: [dma] Fixes for abort handling
justification: The RTL introduces a new parameter NUM_MAX_OUTSTANDING_REQS=1 in dma_pkg.sv and updates tlul_adapter_host instantiations to use it. The DV diff shows that dma_env_pkg.sv previously defined NUM_MAX_OUTSTANDING_REQS=2 locally, which is now removed and replaced with references to dma_pkg::NUM_MAX_OUTSTANDING_REQS. This parameter change affects TL agent configuration (max_outstanding_req assignments in dma_env_cfg.sv), breaking the interface contract between RTL and DV testbench agents.

commit_message: [dma] SHA2 expects big endian data
justification: The RTL now performs byte-lane swapping (big-endian conversion) internally using {<<8{...}} bit-reversal operator. The scoreboard's reference model previously performed this swap explicitly (msg_q[i ^ 3]) and must now remove it to match the updated RTL behavior. This is a reference model desynchronization from behavioral RTL change.

commit_message: [dma] Update address alignment check
justification: The commit moves the dma_transfer_width_e enum definition from DV package (dma_env_pkg.sv) to RTL package (dma_pkg.sv). DV sequences that previously imported this enum from dma_env_pkg must now import it from dma_pkg instead, or risk compilation failures. The enum values themselves remain unchanged, but the import path dependency is altered.

commit_message: [hw,dma,rtl] Add a valid register for the enabled memory range
justification: The RTL adds a new register `range_valid` with offset 0x2c and shifts all subsequent register offsets, requiring manual RAL updates (*_reg_block.sv, *_ral_pkg.sv). The DV sequence in dma_base_vseq.sv now explicitly writes the new `range_valid` register, which must be reflected in the RAL model for correct register access semantics.

commit_message: [hw,dma,rtl] Change the transfer_width encoding
justification: The transfer_width encoding has changed (0b11 is now invalid, 0b10 now maps to 4-byte transfers), which invalidates the enum definition in dma_env_pkg.sv. Existing UVM sequences that reference DmaXfer4BperTxn or generate transfer_width values must now use the new encoding (2 instead of 3), breaking compatibility with sequences written against the old register map.

commit_message: [hw,dma,rtl] Rename RANGE_UNLOCK_REGWEN to RANGE_REGWEN for a better semantic
justification: Register name rename from RANGE_UNLOCK_REGWEN to RANGE_REGWEN invalidates UVM sequences that reference the old register name (dma_seq_item, dma_base_vseq) and requires updates to manually maintained RAL references in the scoreboard and coverage collection. The DV diff shows explicit changes to *_seq_item.sv (mem_range_unlock → mem_range_lock), *_base_vseq.sv (register access), *_scoreboard.sv (RAL field access), and *_cov*.sv, confirming both sequence and RAL desynchronization.

commit_message: [dma] Remove outdated constant `NUM_LSIO_TRIGGERS`
justification: The DV diff shows changes to the interface width parameter definition in dma_if.sv, dma_seq_item.sv, and tb.sv. These files encode explicit knowledge of the lsio_trigger interface width, which changed from the hardcoded `NUM_LSIO_TRIGGERS` constant to the dynamic `NumIntClearSources` parameter. The parameter reference update in dma_if.sv's `WIDTH_IN` parameter and the bit-width declarations in dma_seq_item.sv and tb.sv represent interface drift corrections necessitated by the RTL's parameterization change.

commit_message: [hw,dma,dv] Initial upstream of the DMA DV
justification: This is an initial upstream of DMA DV introducing new coverage infrastructure (*_cov_if.sv, *_cov_bind.sv) that binds to the dma module and samples reg2hw signals. The RTL diff shows a signal type swap (sys_req_t ↔ sys_rsp_t on sys_i/sys_o ports), which breaks the interface contract that DV agents and drivers encode. The coverage bind references specific module hierarchy (u_dma_cov_if bound to dma module) and register signals that must align with RTL.

commit_message: [sram_ctrl,dv] Add readback_regwen test
justification: The DV diff shows enhancement to sram_ctrl_regwen_vseq.sv to test the new readback_regwen register and its interaction with the readback CSR. The scoreboard was also updated to handle the new readback_regwen case. This is a sequence enhancement to cover previously untested register logic, not a breaking change; however, the sequence now has new expectations and dependencies on readback_regwen behavior that must be validated.

commit_message: [sram_ctrl] Expose number of PRINCE half rounds as parameter
justification: A new parameter `NumPrinceRoundsHalf` was added to the sram_ctrl module and must be threaded through the testbench instantiation and environment configuration. The DV diff shows updates to tb.sv (testbench top) and simulation configuration files with the new parameter, indicating interface changes that could break DV components if not properly propagated through the environment.

commit_message: [entropy_src/dv] Change assertions for max rate
justification: The DV diff shows removal of $assertoff statements in entropy_src_rng_vseq.sv that were previously disabling assertions during max rate tests. The RTL diff fixes the underlying issues (rng_valid_bit_cnt_d logic and esfinal_exp_drop replacement), making those assertions valid again. The sequence file had hard-coded references to specific assertion names that are no longer needed after the RTL fixes, and these references must be removed to avoid assertion path mismatches.

commit_message: [prim_ascon_duplex] add TB for prim_ascon_duplex
justification: This commit adds new DPI-C testbench infrastructure and reference model functions (c_dpi_aead_encrypt, c_dpi_aead_decrypt) for the prim_ascon_duplex module. The changes are additions to DPI model files, C source code, and build configuration—infrastructure and tooling—rather than modifications that break existing DV components, sequences, checkers, assertions, coverage, or RAL definitions.

commit_message: [prim_esc_receiver] Register esc_req_o to avoid potential CDC issues
justification: The RTL change adds a one-cycle pipeline register (esc_req_q) to the esc_req_o output, which introduces a latency delay. The DV diff shows multiple testbench sequences requiring timing adjustments: additional wait_clks(1) calls are added in several places, and TIMEOUT_CYCLES timing is adjusted from +1 to +2 cycles. This timing-dependent behavior invalidates existing test sequences that rely on the original combinational timing of esc_req_o.

commit_message: [i2c,dv] Add new types for i2c TLM modelling
justification: This commit adds new type definitions (rw_e, acknack_e enums and i2c_transfer_q, i2c_transaction typedefs) to support improved TLM modelling in the i2c DV environment. The changes are infrastructure/library enhancements that enable cleaner code patterns but do not break existing DV components, invalidate sequences, desynchronize checkers, orphan assertions, regress coverage, or desynchronize RAL models.

commit_message: [otbn,dv] Teach tracer how to emit prefixes for stray changes
justification: This commit modifies the OTBN tracer utility to add support for emitting prefix tags for unexpected state changes. The change is a utility/infrastructure enhancement to the tracing framework itself, not a response to RTL interface drift, sequence invalidation, checker desynchronization, or coverage regression. The tracer is a DV support tool, not a core testbench component.

commit_message: [csrng] Add per-instance internal state read enable
justification: The RTL introduces two new registers (int_state_read_enable and int_state_read_enable_regwen) with associated offsets and register IDs in csrng_reg_pkg.sv. The DV scoreboard adds empty case blocks for these registers, indicating incomplete reference model updates. Register offset changes (0x38→0x40, 0x3c→0x44, etc.) and the new register parameters require corresponding RAL model updates and sequence adjustments to access the new registers correctly.

commit_message: [csrng] Make reseed counters readable at any point in time
justification: The RTL adds three new readable reseed counter registers (RESEED_COUNTER_0/1/2) with shifted memory offsets, invalidating existing register access sequences and requiring scoreboard updates to skip read checks for these new registers. The register map has fundamentally changed, affecting both sequence operability and reference model alignment.

commit_message: [uart] Add new tx_empty interrupt
justification: The commit adds a new interrupt port (intr_tx_empty_o) to the UART interface, requiring updates to the testbench top-level signal declarations and interrupt enumeration. The interrupt sequence test (uart_intr_vseq.sv) now includes a new TxEmpty test case with specific protocol checks, and the scoreboard reference model must predict this new interrupt based on TX FIFO depth. The NumUartIntr count changed from 8 to 9, invalidating hardcoded interrupt masks.

commit_message: [uart] Rename tx_empty to tx_done
justification: The commit renames the tx_empty interrupt signal to tx_done throughout the RTL and DV. The DV diff shows signal name changes in tb.sv (INTERFACE_DRIFT: interrupt wire renamed), uart_env_pkg.sv (enum constant renamed), multiple *_vseq.sv files (SEQUENCE_INVALIDATION: interrupt references updated in virtual sequences), and uart_scoreboard.sv (CHECKER_DESYNC: interrupt prediction logic updated to use new signal name). All DV components encoding explicit knowledge of the tx_empty signal must be updated to reference tx_done.

commit_message: [rtl] MuBi encoding of iCache memory ctrl signals
justification: The RTL commit adds a new .alert_o output port to memory control modules (prim_ram_1p_scr and prim_ram_1p_adv). The DV diff shows corresponding updates to the testbench instantiation (otbn_top_sim.sv) to accommodate the new port, but other DV components that reference the module interface (environment configuration, agents, drivers) may not have been updated to handle or monitor this new alert signal.

commit_message: [keymgr] Reorganize advance call payloads
justification: The RTL reorganizes advance call payloads by reordering which seed values are used in each advance stage (REVISION_SEED moved to Creator stage, CREATOR_ADV_SEED to OwnerInt stage, OWNER_ADV_SEED to Owner stage). The scoreboard's reference model structures and comparison logic have been updated to reflect these payload reorderings, indicating the RTL behavioral change required corresponding updates to the checker's state and output logic.

commit_message: [sram_ctrl] Add readback feature
justification: The RTL commit adds new output ports (wr_collision_o, write_pending_o) to memory modules and new input ports (readback_en_i, readback_error_o, wr_collision_i, write_pending_i) to TLUL adapter instances. The DV diff shows these ports being added to the Verilator testbench simulation module (otbn_top_sim.sv) with unconnected assignments. Other DV components that interface with these modules (environment, agent, monitor) will fail unless they are updated to handle these new signals.

commit_message: [hmac,csrs/rtl] Add key_swap field and expose hmac idle status
justification: The DV diff shows explicit changes to hmac_env_pkg.sv (a manually maintained DV configuration file) with updated register field indices for both CFG and STATUS registers due to the addition of key_swap and hmac_idle fields. These index changes will invalidate any sequences that rely on hardcoded bit positions for register access and require RAL model updates to reflect the new register map structure.

commit_message: [hmac,rtl/dv] RTL and DV fixes for digest loading and error handling
justification: The RTL changed the error handling priority (SwInvalidConfig now has highest priority) and modified digest loading logic (removed inter_digest temporary variable, changed digest assignment order). The scoreboard was updated to match: removed previous_digest_swap tracking, simplified digest comparison logic, and added SwInvalidConfig error prediction at the correct point. The scoreboard's reference model must now reflect the new RTL behavior.

commit_message: [ipgen,flash_ctrl] Delete old files
justification: This commit deletes old DV documentation and infrastructure files (README.md and other legacy DV artifacts) as part of a refactoring effort (#8440). The deletion of documentation and obsolete files does not directly break DV functionality, sequences, assertions, or coverage—it is a cleanup/reorganization activity. No active DV component files that encode testbench logic are modified.

commit_message: [keymgr/rtl] Raise error for any operation in Invalid state
justification: The RTL introduces new error handling behavior (invalid_op signal and alert generation in StCtrlInvalid state), and the DV diff shows the scoreboard reference model was updated to predict the new expected behavior (recoverable alert, OpDoneFail status, invalid_op error code). This is a checker synchronization update where the scoreboard tracks the RTL behavioral change.

commit_message: [keymgr/rtl] Abort into Invalid when Creator Root Key not valid
justification: The RTL diff shows a behavioral change in the state machine logic where keymgr now aborts to Invalid state when the Creator Root Key is invalid (adding a check on `root_key_valid_q`). The DV diff updates the scoreboard's reference model (`get_next_state` function) to reflect this new conditional logic, checking both keymgr enable status and Creator Root Key validity before allowing transition to StInit. This is a classic CHECKER_DESYNC scenario where the scoreboard's reference model must be synchronized with the RTL's updated state machine behavior.

commit_message: [i2c] Prevent transmission until the bus is free
justification: The DV diff shows that test sequences reference internal RTL signal paths that have been reorganized. Start and stop detection logic has been moved from `u_i2c_target_fsm` to a new `u_i2c_bus_monitor` module. Any DV assertions or bind files that directly reference the old hierarchical paths will fail to resolve.

commit_message: [kmac/rtl] Abort when sideload key is invalid during operation
justification: The RTL introduces new error detection behavior (checking sideload key validity in every FSM state, not just StAppCfg) and a new error transition path (StKeyMgrErrKeyNotValid → StError). The DV scoreboard reference model must now account for this expanded key-validity checking logic and the resulting digest output behavior (all-zero in error state). The existing test comment removal suggests coverage expectations have changed but the reference model has not been updated to reflect the new behavioral constraints.

commit_message: [kmac/rtl] Fix four problems in error handling
justification: The RTL changes introduce new FSM states (StErrorAwaitSw, StErrorAwaitApp, StErrorWaitAbsorbed) and alter error handling behavior in kmac_app. The DV sequence `kmac_key_error_vseq.sv` is updated to wait for both valid AND last signals on the HW app interface, reflecting the changed protocol behavior where KMAC now waits for all data items before returning to idle. This is a classic sequence invalidation where the operational constraint (timing of when the FSM exits error state) has changed, requiring the test sequence to be restructured.

commit_message: [kmac/rtl] Move `err_processed` from CFG_SHADOWED to CMD CSR
justification: The commit moves the `err_processed` field from the CFG_SHADOWED CSR to the CMD CSR. The DV diff shows that kmac_base_vseq.sv must update register access patterns (from ral.cfg_shadowed.err_processed to ral.cmd.err_processed) and that kmac_scoreboard.sv must update its reference model to read from the new CSR location. These changes represent sequence invalidation (altered register map access) and checker desynchronization (scoreboard state machine logic no longer aligns with RTL behavior due to CSR relocation).

commit_message: [csrng/rtl] Add reseed interval status error
justification: The RTL introduces a new reseed interval status error mechanism with a CMD_STS_RESEED_CNT_EXCEEDED status response and reseed_cnt_alert_o output, but the DV diff shows only placeholder empty handling in the scoreboard for 'reseed_interval' register reads and a bug fix to reseed_counter initialization (changed from 1'b1 to 1'b0). The scoreboard reference model does not reflect the new RTL behavioral change—specifically, the logic that generates an error response when reseed count is exceeded is not modeled in the checker.

commit_message: [csrng] Add SVAs to check for unexpected pushes to the genbits FIFO

commit_message: [csrng/rtl] Add command out of sequence cmd_sts error
justification: The RTL introduces a new error condition (cmd_sts invalid command sequence) that changes the protocol behavior. Multiple existing test sequences are updated to send UNI (uninstantiate) commands and explicitly check for CMD_STS_SUCCESS instead of raw 0, indicating that the expected command response values and state machine sequencing rules have changed. The scoreboard reference model must be updated to account for the new invalid_cmd_seq_o signal and its interaction with cmd_sts encoding.

commit_message: [i2c] Add configurable policy for target address NACK

The DV diff shows the glitch sequence must be updated to recognize these new states, indicating that existing sequences and reference models encoding FSM state transitions and stretch timeout handling are now invalid or desynchronized.

commit_message: [edn] Harden FIFO instantiations

commit_message: [prim, rom_ctrl] Increase number of PRINCE rounds for improved security
justification: The DV diff shows a parameter change in the scramble reference model (scramble_model.cc) that reflects the RTL's PRINCE round increase from 2 to 3 half rounds. This is a behavioral change to the reference model used by the scoreboard for data scrambling verification. Without this update, the scoreboard's expected scrambled data would not match the RTL's actual output, causing checker desynchronization.

commit_message: [i2c] Add StretchAcqSetup state to preserve ACK setup time
justification: The RTL adds a new FSM state (StretchAcqSetup) to the i2c_target_fsm state machine. Without proper handling, sequences that assume completeness of the state partition would become invalid.

justification: The RTL overhaul removes NACK-specific FSM states (NackWait, NackSetup, NackPulse, NackHold) and introduces a new ACQ FIFO entry type (AcqNackStop), fundamentally changing the target mode protocol flow. The DV sequence (i2c_glitch_vseq.sv) already shows direct adaptation to removed states and altered ACQ FIFO expectations, but scoreboard and reference model logic that tracks NACK behavior and ACQ FIFO entries must be updated to reflect the new state machine topology and NACK timeout handling.

commit_message: [i2c] Eliminate multi-item repeated start entry in ACQ FIFO
justification: The RTL changes the ACQ FIFO transaction recording behavior for Start/Repeated Start symbols—they are now combined with address data instead of being separate entries. The DV diff shows extensive modifications to i2c_base_vseq.sv that restructure transaction generation logic (fetch_txn function), eliminate the two-entry RS handling, and track address matching state ('addressed' variable replacing 'got_valid'). These sequence changes reflect the new protocol semantics and the RTL behavioral shift in how start conditions are recorded, directly invalidating the previous transaction structure and requiring scoreboard reference model updates.

commit_message: [i2c] Doc fixups
justification: The DV diff contains only comment/documentation updates (improved clarity of interrupt handling documentation) with no functional code changes that would break DV components, sequences, checkers, assertions, coverage, or RAL models.

commit_message: [i2c/rtl] Replace FFs for FIFOs with a single SRAM

commit_message: [i2c,rtl] i2c_fsm changes for prediction of target clock-stretching
justification: The RTL change introduces a new FSM state (tClockHigh) and modifies clock-stretching detection logic to use predictive timing rather than waiting for observed scl_i transitions. The DV diff shows constraint relaxation (thigh minimum changed from computed value to hardcoded 4), timing constraint removal (thigh == equation deleted), timeout increase (rd_txfifo_timeout_ns), and transaction generation refactoring. These changes indicate that existing sequences assuming the old timing behavior and scoreboard models tracking the old state transitions are now invalid.

commit_message: [i2c] Reject Start/Stop if SCL changes too soon
justification: The RTL introduces timing constraints requiring SCL to be held stable for at least thd_dat cycles before a Start/Stop symbol is decoded. The DV diff shows multiple sequence constraints have been added and modified (thd_sta > thd_dat + 1, t_buf > thd_dat + 1) to enforce these new timing relationships. Without these constraint updates, existing sequences would generate invalid stimulus that violates the new RTL behavioral requirement, causing sequence execution failures.

commit_message: [flash_ctrl] Share flash_scrambling module among banks
justification: The RTL refactoring moves the scrambling module from per-bank instantiation (inside flash_phy_core) to a shared module at the flash_phy level, introducing new req/rsp interface signals and removing per-bank key inputs. The DV sequence changes reflect hardcoded probe paths that now point to a single shared scrambler module instead of per-bank instances, requiring updates to any testbench code that models or monitors the old per-bank scrambler hierarchy. The interface changes (new scramble_req_o/scramble_rsp_i ports, removal of key inputs from flash_phy_core) may break other DV components that reference the old port signature.

commit_message: [uart] Reduce RX FIFO depth from 128B to 64B
justification: The DV diff shows a critical fix to uart_scoreboard.sv where the RX FIFO depth check was corrected from TxFifoDepth to RxFifoDepth. commit_message: [rv_dm] Implement NDM reset tracking
justification: RTL adds two new module ports (clk_lc_i, rst_lc_ni) for NDM reset tracking with changed reset behavior logic; TB testbench updated but DV environment, monitor, and checker reference models must account for the new lifecycle reset domain and updated ndmreset_ack signal derivation logic to maintain functional equivalence.

commit_message: [usb,aon_wake] Report 'bus not idle' status to usbdev

commit_message: [rv_dm] Implement late debug enablement mechanism
justification: The RTL introduces new input ports (lc_dft_en_i, otp_dis_rv_dm_late_debug_i) and a new CSR (late_debug_enable) with address space expansion (RegsAw increased from 2 to 4 bits). commit_message: [sysrst_ctrl] Rework IRQ sync mechanism
justification: The RTL refactoring reworks the IRQ synchronization mechanism, moving interrupt tracking into the bus domain and replacing the prim_sync_reqack + prim_intr_hw logic with a new sysrst_ctrl_intr module. commit_message: [spi_host,rtl] Factor the byte_sel block into TX FIFO status signals
justification: The RTL change modifies TX FIFO status signal semantics by incorporating byte_select storage into tx_qd, tx_full, and tx_empty outputs. commit_message: [i2c,rtl] Remove double-counted t_f

commit_message: [adc_ctrl] Updates to LP -> NP transition

commit_message: [i2c] Changes to FIFO watermarks and interrupts
