The scoreboard reference model must track 64-bit counter/threshold values and rebuild them from paired register accesses. Coverage points for wkup_thold changed from 32 bins to 64 bins, requiring regeneration.

commit_message: [kmac] Switch to Trivium-based PRNG implementation
justification: The RTL change eliminated the array-based entropy seed interface (NumSeedsEntropyLfsr) in favor of a single seed register, invalidating sequence register access patterns in kmac_base_vseq.sv and breaking the scoreboard's reference model logic for EDN transaction counting in kmac_scoreboard.sv.

commit_message: [spi_device] Fix up TPM command handling
justification: The commit refactors TPM Write FIFO from a dedicated FIFO with read CSR (tpm_write_fifo) to SRAM-backed storage. The DV changes show: (1) tpm_tpm_base_vseq.sv completely rewrites the write FIFO read sequence to access SRAM directly instead of the CSR, breaking the original sequence logic; (2) spi_device_scoreboard.sv removes tpm_write_spi_q and tpm_write_sw_q queues and changes write command handling from queue-based tracking to direct SRAM writes, requiring scoreboard reference model updates; (3) spi_device_env_pkg.sv adds new interrupt TpmRdFifoDrop and adjusts SRAM size parameters, changing memory layout expectations.

commit_message: [usbdev] Introduce Av SETUP Buffer FIFO
justification: The RTL introduces a new 'Av SETUP empty' interrupt and splits the previous single AV FIFO into two separate FIFOs (SETUP and OUT). The DV sequence usbdev_smoke_vseq.sv must be updated to write to the new avsetupbuffer register to keep the SETUP FIFO non-empty, otherwise the interrupt state bits would be asserted and cause sequence failures during cleanup. This represents a protocol/register interface change that invalidates the original sequence behavior.

commit_message: [usbdev] Register changes for separated Av FIFOs
justification: Register field names changed from 'avbuffer' to 'avoutbuffer' and interrupt names from 'av_empty' to 'av_out_empty' throughout register map. All DV sequences that access these registers via RAL (ral.avbuffer → ral.avoutbuffer) and interrupt enumeration constants in env_pkg.sv (IntrAvEmpty → IntrAvOutEmpty) must be updated to maintain structural validity. New register types (avsetupbuffer_reg_t) introduced in autogenerated reg_pkg require corresponding RAL model updates.

commit_message: [edn/rtl] Add new recoverable alert
justification: A new recoverable alert field (csrng_ack_err at bit 13) was added to the recov_alert_sts register, requiring DV sequences that interact with this register to be updated to account for the new field and its bit position. The enum in edn_env_pkg.sv reflects this new alert, but sequences that generate, predict, or verify recov_alert_sts behavior must be revised.

commit_message: [lc_ctrl] Route Flash RMA ACK signals in parallel
justification: The RTL commit changes the lc_flash_rma_ack_i port from a scalar lc_tx_t to a parameterized array lc_tx_t[NumRmaAckSigs-1:0], requiring DV interface update in lc_ctrl_if.sv. Additionally, the FSM module hierarchy changes from a single u_prim_lc_sync_flash_rma_ack module to a generate loop (gen_syncs) with indexed instances plus a new u_prim_lc_sync_flash_rma_ack_buf module, invalidating assertion reference paths in tb.sv that must be updated to target the new hierarchical structure.

commit_message: [lc_ctrl] Always allow transitions into scrap
justification: The RTL change modifies the state transition logic to always allow transitions to SCRAP state and program LcStScrap during the counter increment phase. The DV diff shows scoreboard reference model updates (CHECKER_DESYNC) to predict lc_state_exp = LcStScrap when transitioning to SCRAP, and sequence constraint updates (SEQUENCE_INVALIDATION) in lc_ctrl_smoke_vseq and lc_ctrl_errors_vseq to reflect the new behavioral rule that transitions to SCRAP bypass counter saturation checks.

commit_message: [spi_device] Remove all timing mode CSRs
justification: The RTL commit removes cpol and cpha CSRs from the register map entirely. The DV diff shows that sequences in spi_device_pass_base_vseq.sv and spi_device_tpm_base_vseq.sv previously set these fields via ral.cfg.cpol.set() and ral.cfg.cpha.set() calls, which are now invalid since the registers no longer exist. This breaks both the RAL model (register fields removed) and the UVM sequences that depend on them.

commit_message: [lint,flash_ctrl] Fix some warnings and lint
justification: The DV changes are purely lint/warning fixes: adding missing `default:` cases in switch statements, correcting binary literal formatting (2'b1 → 2'b01), and refactoring a long string literal for line length compliance. These are cosmetic/hygiene changes with no impact on DV functional correctness, interface definitions, sequences, checkers, assertions, coverage, or RAL models.

commit_message: [ipgen,rstmgr] Remove hw/ip/rstmgr and old autogen files
justification: This commit removes the entire hw/ip/rstmgr directory including RTL and DV files as part of a migration to autogenerated sources (indicated by the message referencing ipgen and issue #8440). This is a structural reorganization/consolidation rather than a DV failure mode caused by RTL changes. The DV files are being deleted because the IP is moving to a different location (hw/top_earlgrey), not because of interface drift, sequence invalidation, or other design-verification desynchronization.

commit_message: [otbn,rtl] Refactor loop control so commit doesn't factor into prefetch
justification: The RTL refactoring renamed the internal signal `loop_stack_push` to `loop_stack_push_req` to decouple push requests from commits. This signal name change breaks the DV interface binding in otbn_loop_if.sv and invalidates references in otbn_base_vseq.sv and tb.sv that directly sample this signal.

commit_message: [otp_ctrl] Make secret partition LC lock more generic
justification: The RTL introduces a new generic iskeymgr attribute and refactors the SECRET2-specific lock logic to use this attribute for all keymgr partitions. The DV scoreboard must be updated to reflect this behavioral change: three hardcoded `part_idx == Secret2Idx` checks are replaced with `PartInfo[part_idx].iskeymgr` checks to maintain correct reference model predictions for partition access control.

commit_message: [otp_ctrl,gen] Generate cov_bind and scoreboard files from template
justification: The DV diff shows changes to the scoreboard and coverage bind files that reflect RTL changes: partition name updates (creator_sw → creator_sw_cfg, owner_sw → owner_sw_cfg), addition of HwCfg1Idx, new err_code_10 register, and removal of the uncorr_comp() virtual function. These changes update the DV reference model and coverage points to align with RTL behavioral and architectural changes, but the modifications indicate the files were previously out of sync.

commit_message: [spi_device] Remove generic mode
justification: The commit removes generic mode from spi_device, which invalidates multiple UVM sequences that depend on generic mode configuration (spi_device_abort_vseq deleted, spi_device_fw_init removed). RTL port removals (intr_generic_* outputs) and signal deletions (sram_clk, rst_txfifo_n, etc.) break DV interface assumptions and driver/monitor behavior tied to those signals.

commit_message: [otp_ctrl] Ensure broadcast valid is flopped
justification: The RTL change adds a prim_lc_sender pipeline stage to the broadcast valid signal, introducing an additional cycle of delay. The DV diff updates assertions in otp_ctrl_if.sv to account for this new timing by changing the assertion delay from ##2 to ##3 clock cycles. This is a timing-dependent assertion update required to keep the SVA checks synchronized with the modified RTL behavior.

commit_message: [otp_ctrl] Make ERR_CODE register non-compact
justification: The RTL change converts the ERR_CODE register from a compact multi-field layout (err_code_0 through err_code_9 packed into one register) to a non-compact layout (individual registers err_code[0] through err_code[9]). This breaks register access patterns in sequences (SEQUENCE_INVALIDATION: csr_rd/predict calls now reference individual registers rather than fields within a single register), invalidates scoreboard logic that accesses err_code fields via compact indexing (CHECKER_DESYNC: field indexing changes from err_code_flds[status_err_idx] to per-register access), and requires coverage collection updates to cover all 10 register instances rather than fields (COVERAGE_REGRESSION: cov binning now explicitly lists all err_code[0]-err_code[9] offsets).

commit_message: [otp_ctrl] Add option to disable integrity on a partition
justification: The RTL introduces new partition attribute `integrity` (replacing `ecc_fatal`) and new OTP commands `ReadRaw`/`WriteRaw` for partitions without integrity. The scoreboard reference model must now conditionally invoke `read_a_word_with_ecc()` vs `read_a_word_with_ecc_raw()` based on partition integrity, and error prediction logic is significantly restructured to gate ECC error reporting. Sequences that assume all partitions have ECC/integrity may become invalid.

commit_message: [edn] Move prim_edn_req out of prim
justification: The RTL diff shows module instantiation names changed from `prim_edn_req` to `edn_requester` and instance names changed from `u_prim_edn_*_req` to `u_edn_*_requester`. The DV diff shows a sequence file (otbn_urnd_err_vseq.sv) that hardcodes hierarchical paths for error injection. While the current diff only shows a comment update, the changed module hierarchy and naming will break any sequence or testbench code that references the old instance names in hierarchical paths (e.g., `tb.dut.u_prim_edn_*` paths will no longer exist).

commit_message: [rtl,i2c] Rename FDATA READ field to READB
justification: The RTL field name changed from 'read' to 'readb' in the register map. The DV diff shows updates to both the scoreboard (reference model accessing ral.fdata.readb) and base sequence (RAL field access via ral.fdata.readb.set). These are direct RAL field accesses that must be updated whenever the register field name changes. This is a sequence and checker desynchronization issue, not RAL_DESYNC, because the RAL files themselves are autogenerated from the register definition and no manually-maintained RAL files appear in the DV diff.

commit_message: [otbn,dv] Add ISS support for the lc_ctrl escalate signal
justification: The DV changes modify the reference ISS model (otbn_core_model.sv) to handle a new lc_escalate_en_i signal with lifecycle escalation event support. The model now includes escalation FIFO logic, a busy counter for step optimization, and error reporting via failed_lc_escalate. Without corresponding updates to the scoreboard's expected behavior and error checking logic, the testbench will be desynchronized from the updated reference model behavior.

commit_message: [otbn,dv] Fully Implementing URND PRNG
justification: The commit refactors EDN (Entropy Distribution Network) interface handling in the OTBN model: renaming edn_step to edn_rnd_step/edn_urnd_step, changing edn_urnd_data_valid_i signal to edn_urnd_i/edn_urnd_cdc_done_i, and restructuring model synchronization logic. Existing test sequences that directly call old EDN stepping methods or rely on the prior signal naming and protocol flow will break (SEQUENCE_INVALIDATION). The reference model's internal state machine and CDC synchronization behavior have been restructured (CHECKER_DESYNC), requiring scoreboard/checker updates to match new flush/step/cdc_done sequencing.

commit_message: [clkmgr] Allow software to control clock stepdown
justification: The RTL commit renames signals (byp_req → byp_req_i, adds step_down_req_i) and changes register semantics (extclk_sel → extclk_ctrl with dual-field structure). The DV diff shows corresponding updates to the interface (clkmgr_if.sv: extclk_sel_csr → extclk_ctrl_csr_sel/extclk_ctrl_csr_step_down), sequences (clkmgr_base_vseq.sv, clkmgr_extclk_vseq.sv: variable and constraint renames), and scoreboard reference model (clkmgr_scoreboard.sv: signal and register name updates). These changes span interface, sequence validity, and checker alignment.

commit_message: [keymgr] Fix for error capture
justification: The RTL error capture refactoring introduces a new 4-category error model (sync/async errors and faults) that significantly changes the behavioral semantics of error reporting. The scoreboard reference model must be updated to track fault stickiness and the new error categorization logic (e.g., fault errors now cause invalid operation errors), and existing sequences may generate invalid stimulus based on the old error encoding. Key scoreboard changes include replacing invalid_status_err with is_fault_err, modifying fault detection logic, and updating error code prediction with fault-induced state transitions.

commit_message: [otbn] Operational states and commands
justification: The CMD register changed from a 1-bit signal to an 8-bit encoded command field with enumerated values (CmdExecute, CmdSecWipeDmem, CmdSecWipeImem), and the STATUS register similarly expanded to 8-bit enumerated status values. Any DV sequence that issues commands via the CMD register must be updated to use the new enum values instead of simple bit assertions. Additionally, the STATUS register behavioral logic changed from a simple busy flag to a multi-state status encoding, requiring scoreboard and checker reference models to track the new status states.

commit_message: [flash, top] Merge flash_phy into flash_ctrl
justification: The commit merges flash_phy into flash_ctrl, eliminating the flash_ctrl_wrapper module and fundamentally changing the DV interface. The DV diff shows removal of hdl_path_root configuration and end_of_elaboration_phase logic that was compensating for the wrapper hierarchy. The RTL now exposes internal flash_phy signals (flash_phy_req/flash_phy_rsp) and new ports (mem_tl, flash test interface signals) directly to flash_ctrl, breaking assumptions embedded in the testbench environment that expected the wrapper abstraction.

commit_message: [otbn] Implement illegal bus access error & alert
justification: The RTL introduces new behavioral logic for illegal bus access detection, dummy response generation, and fatal alert triggering that must be reflected in the scoreboard reference model to maintain functional equivalence. Additionally, new register field assignments (illegal_bus_access in fatal_alert_cause) and alert logic changes require sequence updates to exercise the new error paths.

commit_message: [sram_ctrl] Harden initialization counter
justification: The RTL changes introduce dual-redundant initialization counters with a new init_error signal and alter the initialization completion logic. The DV changes update the base sequence to poll ral.status.init_done instead of ral.ctrl.init (SEQUENCE_INVALIDATION), rename alert names from 'fatal_bus_integ_error' to 'fatal_error', update status enumeration (adding SramCtrlInitError), and modify scoreboard expectations for escalation behavior (CHECKER_DESYNC). The scoreboard reference model must now account for the new init_error detection and expanded escalation logic that clears additional status bits.

commit_message: [keymgr] keymgr hardening part 1
justification: The DV diff shows the scoreboard reference model updated to reflect RTL error code naming changes (ErrInvalidCmd → ErrInvalidStates) and new fault handling logic. The RTL introduced new fault_code signals and FAULT_STATUS register, requiring scoreboard updates to track additional fault reasons; this is CHECKER_DESYNC. Additionally, sequences that check error conditions or fault handling may be invalidated by the changed error semantics and new fault status fields, requiring sequence updates.

commit_message: [csrng/sec] create fields to enable functions
justification: The RTL changes the ctrl register from a 1-bit enable field to two 4-bit fields (enable and sw_app_enable), each requiring the sparse value 4'hA. The DV diff shows register access sequences being updated to use the new field widths and values, but this indicates the RAL model was manually updated to reflect the register map change. Both the sequence register operations and the underlying RAL struct definitions were modified to accommodate the new register layout.

commit_message: [otp_ctrl] Split TL-UL interfaces into 'core' and 'prim'
justification: The commit splits the single TL-UL interface (tl_i/tl_o) into two separate interfaces (core_tl_i/core_tl_o and prim_tl_i/prim_tl_o), requiring updates across DV components. INTERFACE_DRIFT occurs because the environment configuration, testbench top, and assertions reference the old port names. RAL_DESYNC applies because the RAL package import changed from otp_ctrl_ral_pkg to otp_ctrl_core_ral_pkg, and RAL parameterization changed from otp_ctrl_reg_block to otp_ctrl_core_reg_block in multiple manually-maintained DV files. ASSERTION_ORPHANING occurs because bind assertions reference the old signal names (tl_i, tl_o) which no longer exist at module scope.

commit_message: [pwm] Wire up integrity alert
justification: The RTL commit adds new alert interface ports (alert_rx_i, alert_tx_o) and an alert_test register to the PWM module, along with new register offsets and parameters (NumAlerts, AlertAsyncOn). The DV diff shows testbench infrastructure updates (alert interface connection via `DV_ALERT_IF_CONNECT` and port wiring in tb.sv) and environment configuration changes (LIST_OF_ALERTS, NUM_ALERTS), but existing register sequences accessing hardcoded offsets and sequences assuming the old register map will be invalidated by the register offset shifts. The new alert interface also requires scoreboard updates to monitor alert behavior.

commit_message: [aon_timer] General register cleanup
justification: The RTL refactoring removed the aon_timer_core_if interface entirely by consolidating register handling into autogenerated files. The DV diff shows corresponding removal of the core_vif virtual interface from env_cfg.sv, env.sv, and tb.sv, including the bind statement. This is a clean interface removal requiring DV component updates.

commit_message: [i2c] Wire up integrity alert
justification: The RTL adds alert ports (alert_rx_i, alert_tx_o) and a new register (alert_test) with associated offsets, requiring DV interface and register access updates. The DV diff shows minimal changes—only alert package parameters and testbench port connections—indicating the testbench is incomplete and sequences accessing the shifted register map are now invalid.

commit_message: [gpio] Wire up bus integrity alert
justification: The RTL commit adds new alert interface ports (alert_rx_i, alert_tx_o) and a new parameter (AlertAsyncOn) to the gpio module. The DV diff shows corresponding updates to gpio_env_cfg.sv, gpio_env_pkg.sv, and tb.sv to wire up these new interface signals and define NUM_ALERTS and LIST_OF_ALERTS. The interface drift is captured and mitigated by these DV changes, but the testbench infrastructure had to be modified to accommodate the new alert interface.

commit_message: [lc_ctrl] Wire up bus integrity alert
justification: The RTL adds a new alert signal (fatal_bus_integ_error) and increases NumAlerts from 2 to 3. The DV diff shows the env_pkg.sv parameter NUM_ALERTS is updated to 3, but the LIST_OF_ALERTS array is incomplete—it still only contains 2 alerts and is missing the new 'fatal_bus_integ_error' entry. This mismatch between the parameter count and the actual alert list will break DV components that depend on the complete alert interface definition.

commit_message: [rom_ctrl] Remove SkipCheck parameter
justification: The RTL removes the SkipCheck parameter from rom_ctrl module and its submodules (rom_ctrl_fsm, rom_ctrl_compare). The DV testbench (tb.sv) instantiates rom_ctrl with this parameter, which is now invalid. Any environment or configuration code that references or passes this parameter will fail elaboration.

commit_message: [dv/pwrmgr] Add smoke test
justification: The DV diff shows structural changes to pwrmgr_if.sv interface definition: signal renaming (wakeups→wakeups_i, rstreqs→rstreqs_i), addition of clk_slow parameter, and multiple new update functions. These changes to the interface contract require corresponding updates in environment classes (pwrmgr_env.sv, pwrmgr_env_cfg.sv) that consume this interface.

commit_message: Revert "[aon_timer] Change escalate_en control to cpu_en"
justification: The commit reverts a signal name change from lc_cpu_en to lc_escalate_en across DV components. The DV diff shows systematic updates to interface definitions (*_if.sv), environment configuration (*_env_cfg.sv), environment (*_env.sv), base sequences (*_base_vseq.sv), and testbench (tb.sv) to reflect the renamed port/signal, which is the classic INTERFACE_DRIFT pattern where explicit knowledge of design interface names must be maintained across DV files.

commit_message: [csrng, top] Connect OTP data to CSRNG
justification: The DV testbench port connection changed from a simple logic input (efuse_sw_app_enable_i) to a structured OTP configuration interface (otp_hw_cfg_i). This breaks the interface contract in tb.sv and requires updates to any DV environment components that directly instantiate or drive the csrng module's interface, such as the top-level testbench and environment packages.

commit_message: [otbn] Add flop to OTBN start signal
justification: The RTL change adds a pipeline stage (flop) to the start signal, delaying it by one cycle. The DV changes update the scoreboard's check_start() logic and tb.sv signal binding to account for this extra latency, ensuring the reference model synchronization logic matches the new RTL behavior. This is a classic checker desynchronization fix.

commit_message: [keymgr, rom_ctrl] Hook up rom digest data to keymgr
justification: The RTL adds a new input port `rom_digest_i` to the keymgr module and modifies the AdvDataWidth parameter. The DV diff shows corresponding updates to keymgr_if.sv (new interface signal), keymgr_scoreboard.sv (new RomDigest field in reference model and verification logic), and tb.sv (port connection). The interface drift is captured in keymgr_if.sv with the new rom_digest signal, and the checker desynchronization is evident in keymgr_scoreboard.sv where the reference model must include RomDigest in the advancement data calculation and validation checks.

commit_message: [otp_ctrl/top] Add external voltage pad for otp_ctrl
justification: A new inout port `otp_ext_voltage_h_io` has been added to the otp_ctrl module interface. The testbench has been updated to instantiate and connect this signal, but DV components like the interface definition and environment package may not yet reflect this new port in their SystemVerilog port lists and signal declarations.

commit_message: [otbn] Implement RND/URND CSR/WSR and RND_PREFETCH CSR
justification: The RTL introduces new RND/URND CSR/WSR registers and stalling behavior tied to EDN requests. The DV diff shows modifications to the ISS model interface (edn_rnd_data, edn_urnd_reseed_complete) and the otbn_core_model to handle RND stalling, indicating that sequences must be updated to account for the new stalling protocol during RND reads, and the scoreboard/checker must be synchronized with the new RND cache and EDN handshake semantics.

commit_message: [otp_ctrl] Align lock bits in otp_ctrl Hjson to use rw0c
justification: The RTL changed register access semantics from W1C (write-1-to-clear) to W0C (write-0-to-clear) for lock bits. The DV sequence was updated to reflect this protocol change: writing 0 instead of 1 to toggle the lock. This is a sequence invalidation where the operational constraint (write value) changed, requiring sequences to be updated.

commit_message: [otbn] Integrate ECC check bits properly into the memory
justification: The DV changes show signal width modifications in the simulation top module (otbn_top_sim.sv): imem_rdata expanded from 32 bits to 39 bits, and dmem signals split into nointeg and full-width versions (ExtWLEN instead of WLEN). These changes to memory interface widths will break DV components that encode explicit knowledge of the original signal widths, such as agents, drivers, and monitors that interface with IMEM/DMEM.

commit_message: [otbn] Fix read/write enables in tracer
justification: The DV tracer interface (otbn_trace_if.sv) adds a new input signal `rf_base_wr_commit` to the interface port list and modifies the read enable logic for bignum registers by factoring in `insn_valid`. These changes represent interface drift where the tracer's explicit knowledge of the design interface must be updated to remain synchronized with RTL behavioral changes.
